Tom / Alana — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so procurement/legal have a clear path: 

1) Scope: 6-month pilot (30k monthly tokens estimate) — pilot will use hosted Redwood API with Dedicated reserved capacity if we scale.
2) Priority legal docs: NDA (immediate), DPA (during pilot), MSA (procurement/legal redline after initial security checklist).
3) Proposed routing: NDA -> security questionnaire / evidence -> DPA -> MSA redline -> PO/commit.

Ask: can you confirm the right procurement and legal contacts and any internal SLA for NDA/MSA reviews? Also, any mandatory clauses (data residency, breach notification timelines, insurance limits) you require upfront?

I’m copying Ben (sales lead) to align on commercial handoffs. I’ll loop Legal once you confirm contacts. I’ve attached our standard NDA for initial review.

Thanks for the context, Irene. I reviewed the NDA and the proposed MSA redline doc. Below is a pragmatic routing plan and suggested turn-times tailored to Medsys' stated expectations: 

Proposed legal routing (detailed):
1) NDA (internal turnaround: 1 business day; external target: 3 business days). Execute electronically (DocuSign) to unblock evidence transfer.
2) Security/DPA parallel intake: While NDA is processing, send SOC-2 summary, architecture diagram, and data retention table to Alana. Laura (Legal) will prepare a lightweight DPA addendum for pilot (focus on subprocessor list, data categories, retention). Target: 5 business days to agree.
3) MSA:
   - Round 0: Redwood sends proposed MSA + redlines (we already have a starting doc).
   - Round 1: Medsys legal returns redline (target 10 business days).
   - Round 2: Redwood responds (target 5 business days).
   - If unresolved, escalation call with Ben and Medsys counsel (target within 3 business days after Round 2).
4) PO/Commercial: Procurement (procurement@medsys.com) issues PO after MSA signature. We should request a soft PO estimate to reserve capacity if possible.

Key clauses to highlight now (please confirm if Medsys flags any of these):
- Data residency / export controls
- Indemnity and liability caps
- Insurance and incident notification windows
- Audit rights and pen-test scope

Proposed owner list:
- Redwood legal owner: Laura Bennett (laura.bennett@redwood.ai)
- Redwood commercial owner: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.ai)
- Medsys legal owner: Melissa Huang (melissa.huang@medsys.com) — Tom to intro
- Medsys security owner: Alana Ruiz (alana.ruiz@medsys.com)
- Medsys procurement: procurement@medsys.com

I’ll prepare a one-page routing playbook and upload to our Drive link for transparency. I also recommend asking Medsys for any non-negotiable clause language up front to shorten the redline iterations.

Attachments: proposed_msa_redlines_2028-07-31.docx (redline stub)

Let me know if this cadence looks good — I’ll draft the routing playbook and DocuSign NDA envelope once Tom confirms Melissa’s contact.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts

Laura / Irene / Ben — thanks for the thorough plan. I spoke with Melissa and procurement; quick commitments from our side: 

- NDA: procurement will review within 5 business days upon receipt (we’ll prioritize). Please send via DocuSign and cc procurement@medsys.com.
- MSA redlines: our legal team expects ~10 business days for the first redline; 5 business days for subsequent responses. If Redwood can limit open items on indemnity and data residency up front, that will materially shorten the cycle.
- PO: Procurement requires signed MSA + statement of work or PO template. Once signed, typical PO processing is 7-10 business days.

I’ll intro Melissa (melissa.huang@medsys.com) on a separate thread today. For now, attaching procurement notes: Medsys_PO_requirements.txt (stub) and confirming our internal stakeholders.

Next steps: Irene — please send NDA via DocuSign and upload the one-page pilot SLOs to the Drive link shared. Laura — once you push the MSA redline to us, we’ll start the 10-day clock.

Thanks,
